text:
夜里突然生病，叫了120送到医院。

这几天因为炎症指标很高，医生说以我目前情况还不能进食，我已经整整七天没吃东西了。

每天就空腹吊个七八瓶水，血管很细又很脆弱。今早护士姐姐给我换针口输液的时候折腾了二十分钟，左拍拍右拍拍这边扎了不行扎那边，最后终于成了，她说：“哎你赶紧出院吧，我都没地方扎了。”

还有个实习护士妹妹巡床的时候问我：“入院的时候体重多少？”我说96，她犹豫了一下问：“是千克吗？”
我说你看呢，感觉她很紧张拿着笔一直没把数字登记上去。我说：是48kg。

有点小可爱。

quotedTweet.text:
『中国尊』被撞，谁最受伤？

小飞机撞击『中国尊』，对中共高层以及对北京人的心理冲击，也可以算一次小微版的『911事件』。
媒体报道说，事故发生于周五（6月26日）傍晚，事发后，这座108层高的摩天大楼上半部出现了一个小窟窿，警方封锁了大楼周围的道路。
第一波受伤害的是『中国尊』、小飞机里的驾驶人员与客户，北京没有报道中国尊大厦里是否有人受伤。
网友通过检索，小飞机上的女驾驶或女客户似乎是中信中高层管理人员，由此猜测与联想，女主角是不是在实施对公司的报复性的撞击，因为公司或公司的某位高管严重伤害了她；
这在中国职场并不鲜见，但只有高管，能够通过飞行的方式，开展一次不失浪漫的报复行为，其他人不是想象力跟不上，是金钱限制了想象力。
第二波受伤害的，是对北京空中管控的空军监测人员，北京城区特别是中南海区域的安全，是一切安全的核心，从中国尊到中南海，在空中也就一脚油门的距离，如果有人携带武器炸药去撞击中南海，那就比911情况更严重，伤害的就不是中国尊，而可能是党国一尊。
从空军最高层到一线监控人员，都要受到严厉惩处，轻则下岗转岗，重则退役甚至以玩忽职守罪论处；
第三波是相关机场，还有所谓的低空经济，有网友提供了时间线：17:30 飞机在北京平谷机场起飞，原计划十分钟后返回
17:40 飞机未返回，并偏航向北京市中心飞行
理论上说，飞机偏离方向，并不是平谷机场的责任，但出了事，就得承担一切责任，不仅此家企业可能要破产，北京周边的全部低空经济都将受到重创或被归零；
还有网友提供了有关部门的通知，可以看出问题的严重性：
各通航企业：
接民航局紧急通知，从现在起对通航开展全面管控。除生产作业、应急救援和121飞行员训练外的所有通航运行全部暂停，恢复时间待定，立即执行。收到请马上回复！！
北京城区去年停飞了所有无人飞机，没人想到，一起突发事件，低空飞机这样针对权贵阶层特殊服务也要被全部停止。
有朋友说蔡奇要倒楣了，我想，蔡奇难被追究，但对老大肯定不好交待，你负责党中央安全，现在出现如此重大纰露，当然是责任难逃，但蔡奇会刀锋向下，对相关企业与北京空管方面领导，将予以严重惩处。

【存储芯片成本大涨，苹果美光打起“口水战”】6月25日，苹果选择在美光公布财报的第二天宣布对iPad和Mac进行涨价，其中，Mac电脑的价格上涨了约15%至20%，iPad的价格上涨了15%至25%。

苹果CEO蒂姆·库克上周在接受《华尔街日报》采访时坦言，这是其“40多年职业生涯中从未在任何领域见过的局面”，他将当前的内存短缺比作“百年一遇的洪水”。他指出内存行业正在将巨额成本转嫁给消费者，苹果公司不得不提高零售价格，因为（苹果公司独自消化增加的成本）这种情况已难以为继。

对于苹果的涨价理由，美光并不买单。美光首席商务官苏米特·萨达纳（Sumit Sadana）在最新一季的财报发布后接受《华尔街日报》采访时，暗指苹果当前因存储芯片供应紧缺而涨价的主要原因是它自己。

Sumit Sadana解释说，在上次存储市场大幅低迷期间，某些客户利用存储价格下行周期极力压低价格。这一举动导致美光蒙受损失，并迫使其在2023年停止产能投资。虽然他没有指名道姓，但从时间和背景来看，显然指的是苹果公司。

在社交平台“X”上有位来自BlueCaptital的匿名投资人以美光CEO的口吻吐槽道，“过去十多年来，苹果一直以5美元的价格购买我们的芯片，把它粘在一个金属盒子里，然后以99美元的升级价格卖给消费者，同时嘲笑我们试图要价7美元。现在我们向他们收取50美元（应该是指256GB UFS存储芯片），他们转头就向自己的客户涨价250美元。” 

苹果并不会坐以待毙，而是积极寻求应对方案。库克之前在接受采访时表示，所有选项都在台面上。

据中新经纬援引外媒报道，为了缓解内存芯片涨价带来的成本压力，苹果正在游说美国政府，希望获批采购中国长鑫存储的内存芯片。（澎湃新闻）

text:
中年女人喜欢被撩吗？

大学同学的妈妈，在我大二那年来学校探望女儿。她穿着公安制服，和我同学迎面走来时，真的英姿飒爽、显得特别年轻。

我当时嘴欠，随口说了句：“海燕，你跟你姐散步呢？”结果她妈妈笑得嘴都咧到后脑勺了。

天地良心，我当时真的以为那是她姐姐，身材好、看起来很年轻。而我那位同学长得胖乎乎的，完全看不出和她妈妈有血缘关系。

因为这件事，她同学好久都没搭理我。直到大二结束，她才告诉我：她妈妈后来经常问起，那个小伙子怎么样了？

岁月如梭，一晃20多年过去了。

前几天我又见到这位女同学，竟然发现她身上开始有点当年她妈妈的影子了！

在这个过程中，有人怀疑苹果把三星和 LG 的技术泄露给了中国。

帖子指出，苹果为了更换代工厂，把本土技术交给了中国。

过去，在美光陷入亏损困境时，苹果曾强势压价，逼迫美光降价。

而当美光靠超预期财报试图恢复元气时，苹果却在第二天就立刻涨价。

而且苹果的涨价幅度远远超过半导体价格的上涨

这篇帖子还解释了为什么半导体市场最后只剩下三星电子、SK 海力士和美光。

像苹果这样的大型科技公司，通过霸凌式采购和放鸽子，把其他竞争者都毁掉了。

帖子甚至声称，AirPods 的制造成本只有 5 万韩元，但苹果却从中赚取了巨额利润率。

Interviewed another candidate today.

I asked him what RAG is.
He replied:
RAG is a technique that allows an LLM to answer questions using external knowledge instead of relying only on what it learned during training.

Then I asked about fine-tuning.
He said:
Fine-tuning is the process of training a pre-trained language model on your own dataset so that it learns a new behavior, style, or task.

Then I asked a follow-up:

Since RAG can inject external knowledge and even mimic a user's persona through retrieved context, why do we still need fine-tuning? When would you choose one over the other?

What would your answer be?

text:
陕西一位00后姑娘，刚刚硕士毕，考上了教师编

成为了一名小学老师。刚开始工作没多久，

她就把自己的《王者荣耀》账号卖了，卖了2200块

结果她转头又通过“账号找回”把号给找回去了

买家联系她，她也爱搭不理

没想到，买家是个较真的人，单程开车将近两千公里 ，跑到陕西报警

警察一看，得，金额够了

于是，现场立案，直接到学校把她带走

她当场吓傻了，辩解说：我还你不就完了

现场有位“叔叔”给她普法，据说她当场，就瘫软了

父母闻讯赶来，痛哭流涕：她才是个25岁的孩子啊

这边买家态度十分坚决，直接放话：我不接受任何调解

也不接受任何解释

想想，一个人能气到开2000公里报警，那得多大怨气

后来，姑娘请了律师，赔了买家2w2，律师费花了3w6

最后，还是被判了八个月有期徒刑，缓刑一年

更惨的是，她背上了刑事案底，这辈子都别想再考公

教书梦也直接断了……

text:
Bayern have rejected a bid worth €5m fixed plus €5m add-ons from Beşiktaş for Alexander Nübel. Bayern are currently demanding up to €20m. The Turkish ckub is offering Nübel a salary worth around €5m net per year including bonuses and an undisputed #1 role. Fresh talks between the Turkish side and the goalkeeper took place on Friday. Beşiktaş and other interested clubs consider Bayern's valuation to be too high, especially that the club is determined to offload him

Two to three weeks ago, Max Eberl informed Nübel's agency that the goalkeeper should not report for the club's start of pre-season training at Säbener Straße. The plan is to find him a new club before then. Nübel has until the beginning of next week to decide whether to accept Beşiktaş' offer. Otherwise, the Turkish club will turn its attention elsewhere. The goalkeeper is considering other options 

Speaking to @SkySportDE, Nübel's agent Stefan Backs said: "We will make the right decision for Alexander's future. What we can confirm is that Beşiktaş are determined to sign him"

[@Plettigoal, @berger_pj]

text:
苹果这波操作真的笑死我了。

事情是这样的：现在 AI 太能抢内存，闹得内存涨价缺货，苹果就借机把 Mac、iPad 全线涨价。库克还甩锅，说这是”百年一遇的洪水”，意思是天灾，不怪我，是内存厂太黑。

结果 Micron 高管当场就不干了，直接开怼：什么洪水？当年把我们价格往死里压、压到我们都不敢扩产的，不就是你苹果自己吗。说白了，今天的缺货，有一半是你当年抠出来的。

但最逗的是苹果想出来的招。它不打算老老实实给 Micron 多掏钱，而是回头去求那个它以前看都看不上的国产厂商长鑫。

嫌弃归嫌弃，真到缺货的时候，还不是得回来求。真香。

xhigh

text:
周末有感：

1. 存储是不到头了，到头不了一点。可以看一下elon musk评价存储和美光，以及明摆着的存储紧缺带来的Q2现货和合约价格暴涨。如果sk海力士下次财报利润是440亿美元，一年利润就是1700亿美元。这是什么概念？ 这接近英伟达的利润了，远超苹果google微软meta的利润。市值才1万亿美元上下。而且后续一直到2028，（甚至2030），这个利润和价格只会增加不会减少。因为HBM4 没有euv根本做不出来，就他们三家能做，三家扩产都很慢，sk海力士算快的了，2027就有龙仁新产能进去。MU更慢，2028才有新的。但2030，最大幅度扩产的海力士也就产能翻倍，5年翻倍，对于agentic AI这样一定要用大量存储的算力结构来说，够么？ 5年才翻一倍？ 3年多前都没有AI….

3. 然后，下半年sk海力士要开始股票回购了，美光年底也要开始股票回购。现在韩股交易量很小，一天交易额大概才几十亿美元，如果sk海力士按照他承诺的，到了100万亿韩币自由现金流后，把自由现金流的一半用于回购股票，一年就算300亿美元，他基本上每天回购的数字是现在每天交易额的20%。

4. 美股IPO. 在美股，1700亿美元的年利润，卡整个算力行业的脖子的HBM王者，发行290亿，然而所有的大厂和产业投资者不会卖，主权基金和养老金长线基金不会卖，流通盘只有小几十亿美元，面对美光相仿量级的800-900亿美元成交量的话，架得住买么？如果几百亿美元成交，很有可能在15天内和spacex一样纳入纳指100，qqq，被动买盘数百亿美元又来了，几个月内也会被纳入费城半导体指数sox，又是百亿美元的买盘。原来韩国人就是钱少，买不起来，整个韩国所有券商账户加上所有的杠杆也就800亿，钱太少了，所以韩国折价，一旦上了美股，等于在穷乡僻壤开的网红小店一下去了纽约时代广场，流动性都不是事儿了。

5. 不知道在恐慌什么。往前看看。7月初，三星会披露预财报数字，7月10号sk海力士美股上市交易，7月底，SK海力士的财报。

以前很看不起本地小模型——太弱，编程根本用不了。

最近看法变了。

当 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的顶尖大模型成为美国人的战略武器之后，一个事实就摆在眼前了：你的隐私，他们大概率都在收集。

我敢赌一把：他们内部一定有工具，能拼出每个用户的完整画像—— 姓名、性别、年龄、城市、住址……

你用得越久，他们越了解你。

而本地小模型的价值就在这儿： 它就在你机器上跑，不联网、不上传，可以安心处理你的提醒事项、备忘录、短信这些最私密的东西。

“能力”和“隐私”这两条腿，缺一不可

text:
婆婆被邻居骂老寡妇的时候，我正好从楼道里出来。

那个邻居是个五十多岁的男人，站在门口冲我婆婆吼：

“你一个老寡妇还占着车位，要不要脸？”

婆婆低着头没说话，在整理垃圾袋。

我走过去挡在婆婆前面：“你再说一遍。”

他愣了一下：“你谁啊？”

“她儿媳妇。你刚才说什么，再说一遍给我听。”

他讪讪地说：“我说她占车位，怎么了？”

我说：“你他妈刚才说的是老寡妇，现在改口了？”

他没说话，转身要走，我叫住他：

“车位是公共的，谁先停谁用。

你再说她一句，我录下来发业主群。”

他走了。婆婆站在后面看着我，眼眶红了。

我说：“妈，以后他再骂你，你打电话给我”。

她说：“不用，我能忍”。我说：“你不用忍，我给你出气”。

从那以后那个邻居见了婆婆绕着走。

婆婆生日那天喝多了，拉着我说：

“我儿子娶了你，是我们家最大的福气。”

我说：“妈，你也是我的福气”。

她被前夫抛弃三十年，一个人带大我老公

从来没人替她出过头。

那天我替她出了，她还不太习惯，但慢慢就习惯了。

现在她叫我闺女，我叫她妈。

我走过去挡在婆婆前面：“你再说一遍。”

他愣了一下：“你谁啊？”

“她儿媳妇。你刚才说什么，再说一遍给我听。”

他讪讪地说：“我说她占车位，怎么了？”

我说：“你他妈刚才说的是老寡妇，现在改口了？”

他没说话，转身要走，我叫住他：

“车位是公共的，谁先停谁用。

你再说她一句，我录下来发业主群。”

他走了。婆婆站在后面看着我，眼眶红了。

我说：“妈，以后他再骂你，你打电话给我”。

她说：“不用，我能忍”。我说：“你不用忍，我给你出气”。

从那以后那个邻居见了婆婆绕着走。

婆婆生日那天喝多了，拉着我说：

“我儿子娶了你，是我们家最大的福气。”

我说：“妈，你也是我的福气”。

她被前夫抛弃三十年，一个人带大我老公

从来没人替她出过头。

那天我替她出了，她还不太习惯，但慢慢就习惯了。

现在她叫我闺女，我叫她妈。

text:
今天遇到一个非常反直觉的问题：
网页、搜索、文本访问都很正常，但视频几乎播不了。
一开始我自然以为是网络、代理、DNS、CDN 哪里出了问题。尤其是 YouTube 播不了时，这个方向看起来非常合理。

但更怪的是，哔哩哔哩也播不了。

这就有点不对了。B 站视频如果也卡，那就不太像单纯的跨境网络或代理规则问题了。

于是开始排查：代理、Surge 规则、DNS、视频 CDN、真实媒体分片下载速度。

结果发现一个很奇怪的现象：

命令行直接拉 B 站真实视频分片是正常的，几十 MB 的分片也能稳定下载。
也就是说，网络其实没坏，CDN 也没坏。

但浏览器里就是播不起来，看起来像一直在缓冲。

最后定位到一个我以前几乎不会优先怀疑的地方：音频输出设备。
当时系统默认输出是外接 Dell 显示器的 DisplayPort 音频。
系统音量读数异常，Chrome 日志里也有 audio output stream 的错误。

把输出设备切回 MacBook Pro 内置扬声器之后，B 站视频立刻恢复播放。

这件事很刷新认知。

原来浏览器里的“视频播放”并不是只要视频数据下载成功就行。播放器的媒体管线里，视频解码、音频解码、音频输出、时间轴同步是绑在一起的。

音频输出设备如果打不开或状态异常，视频时间轴也可能直接停住。

所以这次学到一个排查顺序：

如果视频播不了，但网页正常、分片下载也正常，别只盯着网络。
顺手切一下音频输出设备，尤其是外接显示器、HDMI、DP、蓝牙耳机、AirPlay 这些。
这是我第一次真切遇到“音频输出导致视频播放停止”的 bug。很反直觉，但确实存在。

codex国内使用方法在国内使用

Codex，由于网络环境限制，通常需要借助第三方工具配置国内的大模型服务。

以下是具体步骤：

1.下载并安装必要软件Codex：前往OpenAI官方页面（https://t.co/n0kEuDy8mG）下载适用于Windows或macOS的官方桌面应用。

CCSwitch：从https://t.co/WT4fEisX0Q（https://t.co/h22JJeI46c）下载并安装3.16!1及以上版本，这是一个用于路由AI请求的本地代理工具。

2.获取国内大模型APIKey选择一个国内AI服务提供商（如DeepSeek（https://t.co/s3REd0WGfX）、智谱AI（https://t.co/ELNGbfuoIy）等），注册并完成实名认证。在提供商的控制台创建APIKey，并完成最低充值（通常几元即可满足初期体验需求）。

3.配置CCSwitch打开CCSwitch，在左侧选中“GPT”，点击右侧“+”号添加供应商。选择你注册的大模型提供商（如DeepSeek），将获取的APIKey填入对应字段。

进入CCSwitch的“设置”→“路由”页面，开启“本地路由”总开关，并勾选“Codex”。

4.启动并使用Codex完成上述配置后，退出并重新打开Codex。Codex的请求会通过CCSwitch转发到你配置的国内大模型，即可正常使用。

Judge: “…”

Man: “Fair.”

Judge: “You’re staying mayor.”

Man: “That’s exactly what I was afraid of.”

text:
6 月 26 日，OpenAI 正式从 ChatGPT 中移除了 GPT-4.5。这是 GPT-4 系列在 ChatGPT 里的最后一个模型，至此，GPT-4 时代在消费端彻底翻篇。

我觉得 GPT-4.5 至今仍是最好的写作模型之一，GPT-5 系列在文风和个性上始终没能达到 GPT-4.5 的水准。

GPT-4.5 原本就只对付费用户开放，使用量不大，所以 OpenAI 只给了 30 天的过渡期（5 月 28 日公告，6 月 26 日下线）。已有的 GPT-4.5 对话会自动切换到 GPT-5.5 继续，用户不需要手动操作。基于 GPT-4.5 搭建的自定义 GPT 也将同步失效，创建者需要手动迁移到新模型。

API 端不受影响，开发者仍然可以通过 API 调用 GPT-4.5。

回头看，GPT-4 系列的退场过程颇为曲折。去年 GPT-5 发布时，OpenAI 原本打算同步下线 GPT-4o，结果引发大规模用户抗议，不少人把 GPT-4o 当成了有温度的陪伴者，对下线反应激烈到 OpenAI 不得不临时恢复。最终 GPT-4o 在今年 2 月才正式退役，OpenAI 当时透露日活用户中仅 0.1% 仍在选用它，但按 8 亿周活用户的基数算，这仍然意味着约 80 万人。

下一个要走的是 o3，8 月 26 日下线，过渡期 90 天。

text:
When we partnered with Bubble, their original vision wasn't to build a network of agencies like RapidDev.

It was the opposite: give people the tools to build for themselves.

So when I got asked whether agencies still make sense in a world where AI can spin up software for anyone, I gave the honest answer.

People will always hire vendors.

I was on a walk-and-talk with a guy still selling websites for $10K. It doesn't matter how good the technology gets, there's an asymmetry of information. Busy owners don't want to learn the tools. They want the expert who's done it a thousand times, who knows how to structure a site, write the copy, get it right.

Prices will collapse on the commodity end. That's already happening.

But there will always be clients who want a professional job, and don't mind paying for it.

That's the lane we're doubling down on at RapidDev. And it's why our bet on Bubble keeps paying off.

text:
说些有些人不喜欢听的, 这两天镁光CEO说「苹果前几年5刀内存卖100刀, 涨价到 50刀卖250刀; 压价到把镁光利润干负」, 根本就不像是一个职业经理人说的话.
首先承认那几年苹果 8G 内存选配加 100刀确实很贵, 但对C端卖 SKU 和卖裸片就不是一个逻辑.
很多人都知道 Mac 入门机型实际到手价比官方标价低得多, 导致选配加价比苹果标价还高, 还不如直接选择更高端配置的基础款走其他平台的来的优惠.
其实就说明基础款机型的价格都是被特殊优惠的, 包括到今年 16+512 Air 那个国补后价格其实就是性价比爆棚.
而且要知道, Apple Silicon 本身的架构到今天还是很领先, 加上到今天主流 PC 笔记本都没几个上 3nm 的, 苹果能每年给笔记本用新工艺+新封装, 保持 10-20% 的速度高速迭代, 研发成本可想而知.
而很多人眼里高性价比的 PC, Y-1 Y-2 那种老处理器(比如7840)改名当新品卖的情况早就是常态化, 论各方面产品力的差距就是被 Mac 不断拉开. 甚至可以预计, 到这些厂商库存基本清完, 那价格也得起飞.
至于为什么这么晚才起飞, 还不是因为需求疲弱, 而稍微张点价需求又被压制.
很多人嘲笑 Steam Machine 的高定价, 就是因为 V 社现在的制造模式就是 JIT, 没有库存 RAM 的话那只能卖这个价才有基本利润.
甚至很多人不知道, 苹果的内存, 不管你是 128G 还是 512G 的 Mac Studio, 被一泡水意外损坏了, 他们购入 AC+ 还有后续服务的价格都是一样的.
等于说苹果的内存和存储定价, 就是包括了售后的溢价成本. 当然就以现在的涨价幅度来说, 可能当初的定价都不太够 cover.
现在大家也看到了, 所谓那些年买的便宜 SSD 和内存, 以及还有显卡, 哪怕是自然损坏, 厂商居然会想尽办法拒保, 甚至宁可退钱也不给你修.
而如果翻旧账的话, 镁光说苹果 23 年压价, 但情况是 22 年很多手机厂商以为口罩紧张还在持续, 特别是小米还在做季度 TOP1 后的美梦, 结果一到 23 年初发现制成品起飞了, 开始去库存, 然后镁光等内存厂的订单光速萎缩.
要知道 Fab 里面的机台轨道的运行都是高度编程化的, 包括辅料订货生产都是相对稳定的速度, 如果需求一旦萎缩, 产能缩减会变得非常痛苦, 等于厂商不能大幅度降低产能, 致使生产成本变得像是运营成本, 但生产出来的产品又卖不掉, 再加上内存闪存都是规格通用的产品, 生产端竞价就很激烈, 那镁光的东西让苹果接盘就不错了, 还怨人家那会压价.
当然苹果这波加价肯定也是超过实际物料涨价水平的, 但过了 618 才涨价, 说明苹果已经认为价格敏感人群基本都选购的差不多了, 剩下的客户都是刚需客户.
那要知道 Mac 这玩意现在有多刚需, 我有个做运营的朋友之前还在用老 Intel Mac, 日常出门带个 M3 iPad Air 当电脑用, 结果发现要玩 CodeX 提高工作效率, 或者做副业, 那 Apple Silicon Mac 就是刚需.
甚至最近大家也都知道 MS 开始要加强 Windows 的原生 Shell 能力, 毕竟 WSL2 太重, 而 PS/CMD/PS 的linux alais 基本是几坨屎山; Linux Desktop 又是万年烂泥扶不上墙, 那等于说现在要用 Claude Code 或者 CodeX, 以及用 Xcode 搞 iOS 开发, 那 Mac 就是唯一选项.
所以说 Apple 是有理由认为, 随着 AI 工具流的进一步加强, 苹果能从 Mac 上从用户收 AI 工具税. 
甚至苹果自己的 Apple Silicon 云端算力机房都要用大量算力, 甚至对开发者可以有很大的免费额度去提供给用户, 而不需要其他的复杂订阅条件, 那显然这些钱总是要有来源的.
再说个情况就是, 如果企业也发现要让员工利用 AI 生产力而选购 Mac 的话, 那苹果更有理由加价.
要知道 PC 企业采购市场也是溢价的一塌糊涂, 但产品力远不如 Mac; 苹果在这个阶段改变策略其实基本是出于合理理性.
作为消费者骂骂之前苹果内存贵差不多得了, 今年基础款配置内存加上去, 还能叠那么多优惠, 又是 N2P 工艺新架构新品的 M5 系列早不买, 到了现在涨价了又来骂, 这种人说白了就既没脑子也没钱, 因为但凡有生产刚需, 能创造额外收入/时间节约、对行情有点了解就早下手了.

text:
湖北咸丰这事，听着就让人后背发凉。

一个40多岁的已婚女，找了个小17岁的情人，睡了3个多月。结果女人想回归家庭，小情人不干了，直接把她从13米高的大桥上拖着跳下去，造成轻伤一级。

法院判了：有期徒刑11年3个月。

事情是这样的。张某刚过40岁，风韵犹存，看着身边丈夫越来越力不从心，心里越来越嫌弃。

2025年下半年，她在网上认识了个00后小伙子吴某。一个血气方刚，一个风韵犹存，聊着聊着就聊出感情了。9月份两人见面，该发生的都发生了，从此变成了情人。

吴某迷恋姐姐的成熟韵味，张某被小年轻的活力折服。为了方便私会，张某借故跟丈夫吵架，一气之下住回娘家，天天跟情人腻歪，这一住就是3个多月。

这期间，张某对吴某照顾有加，还时不时给点经济支持，吴某越陷越深。可没有不透风的墙，这事最终被丈夫王某发现了。

但王某没闹，反而找到张某，让她回头继续过日子。毕竟一起生活这么多年，张某对丈夫也有感情，加上王某的包容，2026年初她选择回归家庭，跟着丈夫搬回了家。

这下吴某不干了。才睡了3个多月，还没稀罕够，张某说走就走，他自尊心受不了。他开始跟张某闹，要求她马
上离开丈夫，继续像以前那样跟自己在一起。

但张某铁了心回归家庭，一再拒绝，还要断绝来往。吴某见张某铁了心要甩了自己，开始以死相逼。他开车到一座大桥上，威胁张某如果不离开丈夫，他就跳下去。

张某怕出事，赶紧和丈夫一起去找吴某。见到张某，吴某还是那个要求：离开丈夫，跟我在一起。

但张某已经被他的过激行为吓到了，她本意只是婚外找点刺激，不想捅这么大篓子。加上已经决定回归家庭，所以尽管吴某以死相逼，她还是坚决拒绝了。

谁知吴某突然失去理智，一把抓住张某的衣服，把她拖到大桥边，不顾她挣扎呼救，拖着她一起跳下13米多高的大桥。经鉴定，张某轻伤一级。

审理中还发现，吴某之前还犯过盗窃罪、诈骗罪。最后数罪并罚，法院判他有期徒刑11年3个月，罚金16000元，赔偿张某47000多元。

张某想婚外找刺激，结果差点把命搭进去。吴某年纪轻轻，本来有大好前途，现在要在牢里待十几年。说白了，这就是典型的"玩火自焚"。

这事给所有人提了个醒： 婚外情这东西，碰了就没有好下场。你以为能找到刺激，其实是在玩命。

text:
CNBC types (@JoeSquawk and others) have never properly examined their own investment axioms. 

If they did they’d find the only thing they value is mass opinion. Fitting for a dying industry built on recycling the “wisdom” of crowds. A perverted version of democratic values has seeped into their entire understanding of markets.

This is why they can’t contemplate that bitcoin might be worthless, that NFTs weren’t quite what they were cracked up to be, and that maybe there are better investments than the few chip names one thinks of with >90 P/Es.

Fundamentally they believe the crowd is always right.  An investor who is underweight technology during a technology boom is presumed to have failed. An investor who warns of excess and underperforms for a few years is treated as intellectually discredited. 

CNBC and much of the financial media rarely if ever ask whether the market itself may be wrong; they simply observe performance and declare a winner.

text:
💙🏀💛 THOSE WHO LEAVE….💙🏀💛

Dusty May was never a Wolverine. As it turns out, he was just another run-of-the-mill college weasel.

From the species “Laneus Kiffinitus”. Known for its distinct promissory vocal tones and walking pattern. 

We rescued him from some Dumpwater, FL school where he was quite literally the only thing  of value.  We made  him a national star inside of 2 years. We backed the money truck up for him on a fat new deal….

And how does he repay us? 

By tarnishing the Michigan brand as a mere stepping stone. Something it has never been for anyone until now.

By playing Tarik Skubal reindeer games with his contract. Proclaiming he really wanted to stay, except for the part where he doesn’t leave. 
 
By leaving a sure-fire college dynasty in exchange for what is almost inarguably the worst front office in NBA history. 

The Dallas Mavericks are recognized experts in their chosen field of giving up virtually everything for almost nothing. They gave up the two best players in basketball today for essentially bus-fare to Lubbock. Luka and Brunson (2026 Finals MVP) couldn’t wait to depart Dallas. There was no legacy for them there. 

Dusty May had one of the best jobs in college sports. And today, he gave up the chance to become a true coaching legend. 

The next Wooden. The next Coach K. The next Geno. 

And for what? A few dollars more? 

Huh. Maybe Dusty May belongs with the @dallasmavs after all.

Typing was never a natural way for humans to communicate with technology.

We think in ideas. We speak in complete thoughts. Then we force ourselves to compress all of that through a keyboard, one key at a time.

That friction is frustrating for everyone. But for people with dyslexia, learning differences, physical limitations, or simply a brain that moves faster than their fingers, it can become a real barrier between what they know and what they are able to express.

That is one of the reasons we built Mutter.

Mutter is AI dictation for Mac that does more than transcribe your voice.

You speak naturally, including the pauses, filler words and half-formed thoughts. Mutter cleans it up, understands what you are trying to communicate, and turns it into a polished email, message, note or document wherever your cursor is.

You talk. Mutter writes.

And because privacy matters, Mutter includes a fully on-device mode that can work without an internet connection. Your audio never has to leave your Mac.

No cloud required.
No recordings uploaded.
No sacrificing privacy just to use AI.

Most people can speak roughly three times faster than they type. Mutter turns that speed into finished writing.

We built it for professionals. For founders. For students. For people with dyslexia. For anyone who has ever known exactly what they wanted to say but struggled to get it onto the screen.

The keyboard should not be the gatekeeper between your ideas and the world.

Mutter is free to start.

text:
From new Thoroughbred owner to concerned fan: the sport I love needs us all in the fight. 🐎

Mid-2025 I jumped in as an owner. Early luck brought some wins and a 2026 Derby horse. Now I’m all-in on a strong group of 2-year-olds getting ready to run.

But here’s the reality check: I came in as a passionate fan, not an expert. Watching what’s happening at the macro level is concerning.

Sitting home this Saturday watching the races at Aqueduct — final weekend — I’m seeing the contrast. Decades of history and glory days versus empty stands, FanDuel/TVG pulling broadcasts, track closings across the country, and shrinking foal crops.

This isn’t doom and gloom. It’s a wake-up call!!!!! 

I’m inspired by leaders like @RepoleStable Mike Repole pushing hard for change and challenging the old guard. I’ve met so many great, committed people in this game over the last year. We’re all pot-committed.

What we need now is a stronger collective voice that resonates nationally.

Mid-2025 I jumped in as an owner. Early luck brought some wins and a 2026 Derby horse. Now I’m all-in on a strong group of 2-year-olds getting ready to run.

This isn’t doom and gloom. It’s a wake-up call!!!!! 

I’m inspired by leaders like @RepoleStable Mike Repole pushing hard for change and challenging the old guard. I’ve met so many great, committed people in this game over the last year. We’re all pot-committed.

What we need now is a stronger collective voice that resonates nationally.

It’s time for every one of us — owners, trainers, fans, newcomers — to promote this sport aggressively and back new ideas.

Count me in. Who’s with me? 🔥

text:
The AI Race Will Not Be Won by Gatekeeping the Builders

The question around GPT-5.6 access is not just whether one model should be available today, tomorrow, or “in the coming weeks.” That is the surface issue.

The deeper issue is whether the United States wants to win the AI race by empowering builders or by turning frontier AI into a gated institutional privilege.

There is a legitimate safety argument for limited previews of frontier models. Nobody serious should pretend that increasingly capable systems are risk-free. Models that are better at coding, cybersecurity, agentic workflows, research tasks, automation, and long-horizon planning are also more capable in dual-use domains. A model that helps a security researcher find vulnerabilities can also help a malicious actor reason through offensive steps. A model that helps a biotech researcher analyze complex workflows can also raise obvious safety questions. The frontier is not just a productivity story. It is a capability story.

So a short, structured safety preview is not automatically unreasonable.

The problem begins when “temporary safety process” starts becoming “permanent access culture.” That distinction matters. A phased release can be responsible. A closed club can become strategically self-defeating.

OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 rollout shows the tension clearly. The company described GPT-5.6 as a limited preview of Sol, Terra, and Luna, with broader access planned later. It also said the preview was being limited to a small group of trusted partners after government engagement, while warning that this type of government access process should not become the long-term default. Individual users have no public application path or waitlist. In practical terms, that means the people closest to experimentation — independent developers, small startups, open-source maintainers, researchers outside preferred institutions, and security practitioners without enterprise status — are left waiting. [1][2]

That may be tolerable for a short period. It becomes dangerous if it hardens into policy.

The AI race is not only about who has the best model in a lab. It is about who gets advanced capability into the hands of the most competent builders, who integrates it into real workflows, who creates the best tooling around it, who discovers the failure modes fastest, and who compounds through usage. A model sitting behind a permission wall is not an ecosystem. It is potential energy.

The United States has historically won technology races not merely by inventing powerful technologies, but by letting broad ecosystems form around them. Personal computing, the internet, cloud infrastructure, mobile development, open-source software, and startup culture all benefited from distribution. Builders were allowed to touch the tools, break things, build abstractions, create communities, and push the frontier outward from thousands of directions at once.

AI will be no different.

The core strategic mistake would be assuming that frontier model access is only a safety variable. It is also a deployment variable. It is an education variable. It is a startup formation variable. It is a cyber defense variable. It is a software tooling variable. It is a national competitiveness variable.

When American developers cannot access the most capable systems, they do not simply wait in a vacuum. They adapt. They use older domestic models, open-weight alternatives, foreign models, local models, smaller specialized tools, or whatever can be integrated into their workflows today. That matters because daily usage creates habits. Habits create ecosystems. Ecosystems create standards. Standards create lock-in.

China appears to understand this extremely well.

China’s AI strategy is not only “build a top model.” It is also “flood the zone with usable, low-cost, open or semi-open systems that developers can actually adopt.” The significance of Chinese open models is not just benchmark performance. It is the feedback loop: more users create more integrations, more fine-tunes, more derivatives, more deployment experience, and more trust among developers who want tools they can control. [5][6]

That is why over-gating in the United States could become a strategic own-goal. America might still have the strongest closed frontier model, but China could gain more deployment surface area. In a technology race driven by compounding adoption, that is not a minor issue. The winner is not necessarily the country with the most impressive private demo. The winner is the country whose tools become the default substrate for builders.

There is a familiar pattern in technology: the best tool does not always win. The tool that is available, cheap, extensible, understandable, and widely adopted often wins.

This is especially true for developers.

Developers do not build around vague promises of future access. They build around what they can test, script, automate, debug, and deploy now. They need APIs. They need stable pricing. They need model behavior they can learn. They need rate limits they can plan around. They need documentation. They need repeatability. They need confidence that the tool they are integrating today will not be arbitrarily restricted tomorrow.

If a frontier model is powerful but inaccessible, it does not teach the market how to use it. It does not generate plugins. It does not produce new workflows. It does not create the same open-ended experimentation that happens when thousands of builders start applying it to problems no central lab would have predicted.

This is where policymakers often misunderstand software. Software progress is not only top-down research. It is bottom-up discovery. The long tail matters. The weird hobby project matters. The open-source maintainer matters. The solo developer matters. The small team building something unfashionable matters. Tooling ecosystems are often created by people who were not on anyone’s list of “trusted partners.”

That does not mean every person should get unrestricted access to every frontier capability on day one. It means the release strategy should be designed around broadening access as quickly and safely as possible, not preserving access for a favored inner circle.

The safety case is real, but safety through indefinite restriction has limits. Restricted access can reduce immediate misuse, but it can also reduce legitimate defensive use. Cyber defenders need strong models too. Independent researchers need strong models too. Small companies with limited security teams need strong models too. If the best tools are withheld from the people defending smaller systems, the result may be a security gap where only large institutions get frontier-grade assistance while everyone else remains underpowered.

That is backwards.

A strong safety strategy should not be simply “keep the model away from people.” It should be tiered access, capability-specific safeguards, abuse monitoring, red-team partnerships, researcher channels, cyber-defense safe harbors, transparent release criteria, and hard deadlines for moving from preview to broader availability. It should distinguish between dangerous enablement and legitimate high-leverage work. It should not treat the entire developer ecosystem as a risk category.

The overreach problem also affects the public narrative around AI.

A lot of skepticism toward AI is not actually skepticism toward the tools. It is skepticism toward the messaging. People are tired of being told that fundamentals no longer matter. They are tired of hearing that models replace engineering judgment, architecture, debugging skill, product sense, security discipline, and taste. They are tired of watching shallow demos get marketed as if they invalidate the craft.

That criticism is healthy.

AI does not remove the need for fundamentals. It raises the reward for having them.

A developer with strong fundamentals can use AI to move faster, explore alternatives, generate scaffolding, test assumptions, automate repetitive work, and reason through unfamiliar systems. A developer without fundamentals can use the same AI to create a bigger mess, faster. The model can produce code, but it cannot guarantee that the system design is sound. It can explain errors, but it cannot replace the judgment required to know which tradeoffs matter. It can accelerate implementation, but it cannot give a team taste, discipline, or long-term architectural restraint.

This is why broad access matters for quality, not just speed. The more serious builders who can work with frontier models, the faster the field learns what these systems are actually good for. Real developers discover the edge cases. Real security researchers find the weak points. Real teams learn where agentic coding helps and where it creates hidden complexity. Real usage is not merely consumption. It is evaluation.

A small approved partner pool cannot substitute for the collective intelligence of the broader builder ecosystem.

That is the danger of confusing control with leadership. Control can reduce uncertainty in the short term, but leadership in software usually comes from ecosystem gravity. The United States should not aim to have the most impressive model locked behind the most careful gate. It should aim to have the strongest, safest, most widely used AI development ecosystem in the world.

That requires a different posture.

First, limited previews should be time-bound. If the government or a lab wants a safety window, define the window clearly. Thirty days is very different from an indefinite “soon.” Builders can plan around dates. They cannot plan around vibes.

Second, access criteria should be transparent enough to trust. Nobody expects every security detail to be public, but the broad rules should be understandable. If access is limited because of cyber capability, say what category of risk is being mitigated. If certain capabilities require stricter controls, separate those capabilities instead of restricting the entire model as a blunt instrument.

Third, domestic developer access should be treated as a national asset. Startups, independent developers, universities, open-source maintainers, and cyber defenders should not be afterthoughts. They are part of the competitive base. If the United States wants AI leadership, it needs more people building with frontier tools, not fewer.

Fourth, America needs a serious open ecosystem strategy. That does not mean every frontier model must be open-weight. It does mean the United States cannot allow open development to become a space dominated by Chinese models by default. There should be strong open models, strong open tooling, strong evaluation infrastructure, and serious support for the maintainers who make AI usable outside elite companies.

Fifth, safety should be measured against real-world tradeoffs. Blocking access has costs. Delaying access has costs. Restricting cyber defenders has costs. Slowing small companies has costs. Driving developers toward foreign open models has costs. A mature policy should weigh those costs instead of pretending restriction is always the safer option.

The United States still has enormous advantages: leading labs, deep capital markets, cloud infrastructure, chip design strength, major software platforms, elite universities, and a culture that still rewards ambitious technical entrepreneurship. But advantages can be wasted. The fastest way to waste them is to make the best tools hard to reach for the very people most likely to turn them into the next wave of products, workflows, defenses, and companies.

China does not need to surpass the United States in every frontier benchmark to gain ground. It can gain ground by being more available, more adaptable, cheaper, and more embedded. If American frontier AI becomes synonymous with closed access and institutional gatekeeping, then Chinese alternatives become more attractive not necessarily because they are better, but because they are usable.

That should worry anyone who cares about U.S. AI leadership.

The answer is not reckless release. The answer is not pretending safety concerns are fake. The answer is not giving every capability to every user with no monitoring, no policy, and no accountability.

The answer is disciplined openness.

Short safety previews are defensible. Permanent gatekeeping is not. The former can help manage risk. The latter can weaken the ecosystem that gives the United States its strategic edge.

The AI race will not be won by hiding the best tools from builders. It will be won by giving responsible builders access, teaching them how to use these systems well, preserving the fundamentals that make software reliable, and creating an ecosystem where frontier capability compounds through real work.

The country that wins AI will not simply be the country with the most powerful model.

It will be the country that puts powerful models into motion. 🇺🇸

text:
The dosing risk almost nobody warns you about with grey-market peptides isn't underdosing or fake products, it's getting overdosed.

We collected every third-party Certificate of Analysis we could find on these compounds: 22,588 of them. 15,167 report a measured dose against the stated label. 

So, when you buy, are you getting the dose on the vial?

Mostly, you're close. And when you're not, you usually get more than you paid for, not less.

Across all 12 compounds we track, 44% to 67% of vials land within 10% of label. The rest miss, and the misses skew high. In every compound, over-filled vials outnumber under-filled ones.

Direction isn't the whole story. Over-fills are common but shallow, typically 15 to 21% above label. Under-fills are rarer but cut deeper; the worst run 25% or more below what the vial claims.

From the data:
- Retatrutide is cleanest: 67% within label, 10% short.
- CJC-1295 is worst: 44% within label, 30% over, 26% short.
- Tesamorelin runs 17% short, by a median 26% when it does.
- MOTS-c over-fills 52% of the time and almost never under.

BLOWBACK ON THE OKC COVER-UP
Highlights from my OKC bombing investigation: How two heavyweights in the Clinton Justice Department — both future AGs — helped shield the identity of the accomplice who rode next to Timothy McVeigh in the bomb truck. 

Full post here https://t.co/iIFkKNZCdb 

The receipts are in the book https://t.co/R6mOJudnVR

quotedTweet.text:
𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐨𝐧 𝐉𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐃𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐊𝐂 “𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐞-𝐖𝐨𝐥𝐟” 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲
My book Blowback documents how powerful figures inside the Clinton-era Justice Department worked to lock in the official story that Timothy McVeigh acted alone — even as growing evidence pointed to a larger FBI sting operation that had gone badly wrong.

Here are some of the key moves that helped bury the truth:

• 𝐌𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐤 𝐆𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝, who managed the case from Washington, steered the prosecution to focus almost exclusively on McVeigh, despite multiple eyewitnesses seeing a second man in the bomb truck with him. The night before Garland’s appearance at McVeigh’s preliminary hearing in Oklahoma, he was meeting with First Lady Hillary Clinton at the White House.

• The FBI took possession of surveillance videotape showing the second suspect (“John Doe 2”), but the Justice Department has spent nearly two decades and millions of dollars in court fighting to keep that video hidden from the public.

• Federal informant 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐨𝐥 𝐇𝐨𝐰𝐞, who had been embedded inside the bomb plot, warned that Oklahoma City was a target. When she tried to go public, the government prosecuted her on terrorism charges (which a jury quickly threw out). The McVeigh trial judge then ruled her testimony about the wider plot “irrelevant.”

• When the suspicious 1995 prison murder of Kenneth Trentadue sparked national attention, 𝐄𝐫𝐢𝐜 𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫 was tapped to run damage control with the Senate Judiciary Committee. Promised hearings never happened. The prisoner’s brother, attorney Jesse Trentadue, later linked the murder to the bombing case.

• Years later, when former FBI informant 𝐉𝐨𝐡𝐧 𝐌𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐰𝐬 came forward and connected the bombing to the FBI’s rogue PATCON infiltration program — which he claimed was run out of the Clinton White House — the Justice Department pressured Newsweek to remove all references to PATCON and McVeigh from his story just before publication.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧 𝐢𝐬 𝐜𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫: At multiple critical points, senior Justice Department officials chose to protect the lone-wolf narrative rather than pursue evidence of a wider bombing conspiracy.

President Clinton had promised that “justice for these killers will be certain, swift, and severe.” Instead, key elements of the operation appear to have been shielded from serious scrutiny.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐩𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐁𝐥𝐨𝐰𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤. https://t.co/R6mOJucQ6j

[Photos: Merrick Garland, Eric Holder, Murrah Building], Blowback]
